title: Raft consensus laboratory
objective: Predict when a Raft cluster can elect a leader and commit writes, and explain why it needs a majority.
summary: An intro video shows a write committing on a majority, a five-server simulation lets the learner fail servers and send writes, a guided walkthrough pauses during a leader failure, deep dives explain split brain and cluster sizes, and a final video connects the rules.

props.title: Five-server Raft cluster
props.intro: Fail servers, change latency, send writes and step the clock.

checkpoints.prompt: In one sentence: why does the leader wait for a majority before it commits a write?
checkpoints.explanation: A majority stores the entry before it commits, and any later majority overlaps it, so the next leader always meets a server that has the entry.

checkpoints.prompt: The leader just crashed. What do the followers do first?

choices.text: Wait for an election timeout, then one becomes a candidate
Keep committing writes without a leader
choices.misconception: Thinks followers can commit without a leader

choices.text: Immediately crown the server with the lowest id
choices.misconception: Thinks Raft elects by server id instead of by votes after a random timeout

checkpoints.explanation: Followers notice the failure only when heartbeats stop and their election timer expires. The first to time out becomes a candidate for a new term and asks the others for votes.

checkpoints.prompt: In the simulation, fail servers and send a write until the write cannot commit. How many live servers are left then?

goal.hint: Fail three servers, press Send write, then press Step a few times.

checkpoints.explanation: With two of five servers alive there is no majority of three, so no leader can be elected and the write stays pending. Nothing wrong is committed; the cluster just waits.

checkpoints.prompt: A cluster has four servers. How many can fail while it still commits writes?

choices.misconception: Thinks half the servers is a majority
Thinks one live server can commit alone

checkpoints.explanation: A majority of four is three. With one failure three servers remain, which is a majority; with two failures only two remain, which is not.

checkpoints.prompt: Why can two leaders never win the same term in Raft?

choices.text: Each server votes once per term and a leader needs a majority
Servers with higher ids override others

choices.misconception: Thinks clients take part in elections

checkpoints.explanation: Two majorities of the same cluster overlap, and the shared server votes only once per term, so only one candidate can collect a majority in a term.
